answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake before it can influence decisions, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to have double-voted or colluded across supposedly independent groups. A haven for honest newcomers can keep the stake modest, while delayed withdrawals make rapid identity cycling costly. The attacker must lock up real capital for every fake agent and risks losing it, so a cedar-and-terrace network of fabricated personas cannot gain influence for free.
